note: LIVE DATA — bulk companion to goinggone-lots-real.json; together they are the source for the lots in goinggone.html. Same rule: nothing invented. Every price was read off a live retailer's category page on the date given. Harvested in bulk (one fetch yields 12-15 priced products) rather than one item at a time, so the notes are thinner — but the prices are read from the page rather than summarised from a guide, which makes most of them BETTER evidenced than the hand-researched half. AFTER EDITING, run `node scripts/build-goinggone-lots.js` to re-embed. RULE: a lot's name and desc must NEVER state or hint at the price — the whole game is guessing it. No dollar amounts, no spelled-out prices, no 'four grand', and no comparisons either ('costs more than a car', 'the cheapest lot here'); unit/goinggone.test.js fails on any of them.
method: Fetch a retailer category or search page, ask for the products spanning the widest price range, keep the ones whose price a person could not guess from the shape of the object. Discard size variants of the same item — twelve pizza ovens differing only in deck count are one lot, not twelve.

apparentField.meaning: Editorial judgement — NOT a researched figure — of how the item's real price compares to what a person would guess from looking at it.
apparentField.low: looks cheap, is expensive (the surprise goes up)
apparentField.high: looks expensive, is cheap (the surprise goes down)
apparentField.fair: roughly what you would guess — filler, keeps the game honest

sourcesThatWork: webstaurantstore.com — /search/<term>.html returns 15 priced products; enormous breadth within foodservice
trafficsafetystore.com — category pages; road furniture, excellent $1-100 band
surpluscenter.com — industrial surplus; the cheap end
roguefitness.com — SPORTING. Category pages, superb price spread ($15 change plate to $11,395 treadmill on adjacent pages)
armysurpluswarehouse.com — EX-ARMY SURPLUS. Homepage lists priced products; deep category paths 404, so use the homepage and search
accio.com — marketplace aggregator; noisy, medium confidence at best
adafruit.com — MAKING/ELECTRONICS. /category/<id> pages, with images; goes down to $0.50, the best bottom-band source found
sparkfun.com — MAKING/KITS. /kits and category pages, with images
prusa3d.com — 3D PRINTERS. /category/3d-printers/ lists every model with price and image
mrsolar.com — HOME POWER. /solar-panels/ /inverters/ /batteries/ all list products with prices and images
sourcesThatBlock: govplanet.com (category pages carry no prices in the HTML — auction listings are behind JS)
matterhackers.com (category pages carry no product data)
rockler.com (category pages carry no product data)
signaturesolar.com, altestore.com (product grids rendered by JS)
penntoolco.com (404) — home-shop machinery still has no working source

researchLog.learned: Bulk harvesting works and is roughly 15x faster per item than one-search-per-item, but only four retailers allow fetching at all (list above). Measured rate: 4 category fetches yield ~48 priced products, of which ~12-16 are genuinely DISTINCT lots — the rest are size variants of one object. Reaching 1000 distinct lots therefore needs ~250-300 category fetches, and from the four available domains the result would skew heavily to catering and industrial equipment.

The best lots come in PAIRS from the same category page — the $104.99 hot dog roller and the $4,084.85 one, the $189.99 candy floss machine and the $2,209 one. Same object, same photo, 20-40x the price. Ask each category page for its widest price range rather than its most typical product.

Second bulk harvest (+98 lots, 16 category pages). New working pages: webstaurantstore searches for spiral-dough-mixer / combi-oven / kegerator / slushy-machine / ice-cream-dipping-cabinet / waffle-maker / commercial-blender / chocolate-tempering-machine / meat-grinder / holding-cabinet / walk-in-cooler / french-fry-cutter / coffee-roaster / food-processor / dough-sheeter / shopping-basket; adafruit /category/8 (tools) and /category/105 (Raspberry Pi); surpluscenter /Hydraulics/Hydraulic-Pumps/; trafficsafetystore /traffic-cones. 404s: roguefitness /power-racks-rigs and /rigs-racks (only /conditioning and /weightlifting-bars-plates resolve), trafficsafetystore /radar-speed-signs and /barricades, surpluscenter /Winches/, mrsolar /solar-panel-kits/ and /charge-controllers/. Gotchas: webstaurantstore coffee-roaster search returns mostly coffee (but surfaced the Giesen W6A roaster); gold-flatware prices are per-piece-by-the-case and too ambiguous to use; surpluscenter grid images are lazy-loading placeholders, so pump lots ship without photos.

Third bulk harvest (+94 lots, 24 pages). New webstaurantstore searches that work: stanchion / hand-dryer / rotisserie-oven / bakery-display-case / donut-machine / conveyor-toaster / milkshake-machine / crepe-maker / sushi-display-case / chafing-dish / pizza-delivery-bag / wok-range / pasta-machine / salamander-broiler / hot-dog-cart / cocktail-shaker / butcher-block / mop-bucket. Also prusa3d /category/filament/, adafruit /category/65 (wearables), trafficsafetystore /traffic-signs (parent category lists priced signs), surpluscenter /Hydraulics/Hydraulic-Motors/, sparkfun /kits re-sweep (3 kits not caught first time). Notable finds: live lobsters by the 25 lb case (the price is for the whole case, unambiguous); the search "lobster-tank" returns lobsters, not tanks; "gumball-machine" returns nothing at all. The over-band keeps gaining comedy: an $81k rotating bakery oven, a $55k Mongolian BBQ range, a $25k gnocchi machine.

Fourth bulk harvest (+87 lots, 21 pages). Working: webstaurantstore searches sous-vide / churro-machine / parmesan-wheel (3 results incl. a REPLICA parmesan wheel priced near the real quarter wheel) / red-carpet (surfaced a red-carpet STAGE and choral risers) / meat-saw / sausage-stuffer / panini-press / salad-spinner / bread-slicer / wine-refrigerator (grid shows no images) / chiavari-chair / cash-drawer / steam-table / waffle-cone-maker / espresso-grinder / knife-sharpener / housekeeping-cart / beer-keg; adafruit /categories INDEX page lists every category id (robotics=227, sensors=35, wireless=112, power=44...), then /category/227 and /category/35 both harvest cleanly. Dead: webstaurantstore searches absinthe-fountain, turnstile, gumball-machine (no results); popsicle-mold returns per-each-in-pack pricing (ambiguous, skipped all but one); surpluscenter /Pneumatics/ 404s (only /Hydraulics/<subcategory>/ shapes resolve). Trap to remember: a $0.10 wood bagel miter rounds to $0 and the build drops it — sub-50-cent items cannot be lots.
